content.value_statement: Building reliable LangChain systems is difficult when agents, chains, memory, and retrieval interact. This skill guides architecture choices, patterns, testing, and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains agents, chains, memory, document processing, and callbacks.
Provides starter LangChain Python examples for agents, RAG, chains, memory, callbacks, testing, caching, batching, and streaming.
Compares memory types for short chats, long chats, sliding windows, entity tracking, and semantic retrieval.
Outlines production checks for error handling, logging, rate limits, validation, and observability.
Identifies common LangChain pitfalls around tool selection, retrieval quality, context limits, and agent failures.
limitations: It is a Markdown guide, not a runnable project scaffold.
Referenced resource files are not included in this package.
Examples may need updates for the installed LangChain version and provider SDK.
It does not replace security review for tools that call external APIs or internal systems.

use_cases.title: Plan an Agent-Based Assistant
use_cases.description: Map tools, memory, callbacks, and execution flow before building a LangChain agent.

use_cases.title: Design a Retrieval Workflow
use_cases.description: Choose document loaders, chunking, embeddings, vector storage, retrievers, and answer generation patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Check logging, token costs, validation, rate limits, error handling, and observability for an LLM application.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the LangChain architecture skill to explain which components I need for a chatbot with memory and search. My constraints are: [constraints].

prompt_templates.title: Choose Memory Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare LangChain memory options for this application: [application]. Recommend one strategy and explain tradeoffs for context length, cost, and accuracy.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LangChain RAG workflow for [documents] and [users]. Include loaders, splitting, embeddings, retrieval, source handling, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LangChain application plan for production readiness: [plan]. Identify missing controls for errors, logging, tool safety, rate limits, and observability.

output_examples.input: Design a customer support RAG assistant for policy documents.
output: Recommended architecture: document loader, chunking strategy, embeddings, vector store, retriever, answer chain, and source display.
Validation focus: answer accuracy, retrieval relevance, missing source handling, and escalation paths.
Production checks: logging, token monitoring, rate limits, and fallback behavior.

output_examples.input: Choose memory for a long-running sales assistant.
output: Use summary memory for long conversations and window memory for recent details.
Track key entities separately when customer names, accounts, and preferences must persist.
Set retention limits and review sensitive data handling before deployment.

output_examples.input: Review a LangChain agent that can search data and send email.
output: Confirm tool descriptions are narrow and permissioned.
Require human approval before sending external messages.
Add callbacks for action logging, error handling, and latency monitoring.

best_practices: Define agent tools with narrow permissions, clear descriptions, and validation rules.
Choose memory based on conversation length, privacy needs, and retrieval requirements.
Add observability, error handling, rate limits, and cost tracking before production use.
anti_patterns: Giving agents broad tool access without approval or audit logging.
Storing full conversation history indefinitely without privacy controls.
Deploying retrieval workflows without testing chunking, source quality, and failure cases.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps plan LangChain applications that use agents, chains, memory, retrieval, callbacks, and production controls.

faq.question: Does it generate a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples, but you still implement and test your project.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this useful for RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers document loading, splitting, embeddings, vector stores, retrievers, and source-aware question answering.

faq.question: Does it cover production concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for logging, token monitoring, latency, error handling, rate limits, validation, and observability.

faq.question: What should I check before using the examples?
faq.answer: Verify your LangChain version, provider SDK, credentials, tool permissions, and data privacy requirements.
